intent: Two colonial border lines that disagree, and the strange result: one triangle both Egypt and Sudan claim, and one patch of desert neither will touch, because claiming it means giving up the other.
pacing_profile: documentary: cold open, place, why in 2–5 beats, twist, close answers the open, short CTA (docs/STORY_GUIDELINES.md §2)
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses.
title: The land nobody wants

lines.direction: the opening line, cold — the map is already moving
lines.text: Between Egypt and Sudan there is a piece of desert that nobody claims. Not forgotten. Refused.
In 1899 Britain drew the border along the twenty-second parallel. A straight line, east to west.

lines.direction: the 1902 administrative line draws on 'second'; the two bends pulse on north / south
lines.text: Three years later it drew a second line, following the tribes instead: a bend north by the sea, a bend south in the desert.

lines.direction: the coastal triangle lights on 'coastal'; the disputed plate is on screen with it
lines.text: Egypt holds to the straight line. Sudan holds to the second. Each line gives its owner the big coastal triangle, the one with the Red Sea and the towns.

lines.direction: tighten onto Bir Tawil; the void fills; counter on the area
lines.text: And the same two lines leave this smaller patch to the other side. Claim it, and you accept the line that loses you the coast. So neither does.

lines.direction: answer the opening line with the same noun
lines.text: Two thousand square kilometres of desert, unclaimed on purpose, because wanting it would cost the coast.

lines.direction: short follow — the outro visual does the work
lines.text: Follow for a new map story every day.
